messages:
sara: Quick sync — PM (mike) asked for a single dashboard showing on-prem metrics-export health + per-tenant egress/quota usage. Need runtime/infra/security input on what agent telemetry we can rely on and how it maps to console widgets.

mike: adding context — enterprise sales want SLA-style visibility: last-export, backlog bytes, last successful handshake (kms sig), per-tenant daily bytes and quota consumption. Not asking for message payloads, just metadata.

dan: basic constraints: most customers only allow outbound 443/HTTPS and often via a corporate proxy. We should aim to keep agent egress to a single FQDN and support proxy env vars + mTLS to avoid extra firewall rules.

jana: agree. runtime can expose compact export metrics: export_attempts, export_successes, last_export_ts, queued_bytes, current_backlog_bytes, last_kms_sig_ts. We should keep labels low-cardinality: {tenant_id, agent_version, region}.

leo: security note — if we show last_kms_sig_ts in dashboards, ensure we don't surface key IDs or signed tokens. Audit hooks must emit an audit entry whenever the agent establishes a TLS/mTLS session and whenever a key operation happens. These audit events should be pushed to the customer's audit-log endpoint and our admin telemetry (signed).

anya: for console UX — we need a mapping document mapping agent metrics to widgets. Example: a small sparkline for queued_bytes, a status indicator derived from last_export_ts (green/yellow/red), and quota gauge for daily_bytes vs quota. We also need sample queries for the backend metrics store.

tom: ops question — do we want agents to push aggregated per-tenant deltas or raw per-request metrics? Aggregated deltas reduce egress and simplify quotas calculation. Proposal: agent emits a daily_delta metric every 5 minutes + immediate error events (retry, handshake failure).

sara: sounds good. dan/leo — can we support both direct TLS to export.redwood.com and proxied mode? And what about pinning IP vs DNS? Customers hate static IP whitelists.

dan: support both. Recommend DNS + SNI so customers whitelist export.redwood.com only. If they insist IPs, we can publish an ASN range but prefer DNS. Proxy support via standard env vars (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) + a CONNECT tunnel for TLS.

leo: KMS integration: agent should sign a short-lived export manifest with the customer KMS (or KMS proxy). We must log a corresponding audit entry locally and send a signed audit envelope to the customer's audit endpoint. Minimal info: {tenant_id, export_ts, manifest_hash, sig_meta}. Do NOT include specimen data.

anya: small UX ask from devex — include a sample agent config block that we can paste into quickstart and a minimal dashboard json for the console to import. Developers appreciate copy/paste.

sara: putting a draft sample here so devex can iterate:

```yaml
agent:
  export:
    endpoint: https://export.redwood.com/telemetry/v1
    use_mtls: true
    proxy: ${HTTPS_PROXY:-}
    auth:
      method: kms-signed-manifest
      manifest_ttl: 300s
  telemetry:
    aggregate_interval: 300s
    emit_labels: [tenant_id, agent_version, region]
    metrics:
      - queued_bytes
      - export_attempts
      - export_successes
      - last_kms_sig_ts
```

and a sample firewall note (to add to docs):

```bash
# allow egress to export.redwood.com over TLS
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d export.redwood.com --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# OR, if using proxy, allow corporate proxy host:443
```

jana: on the backend mapping side — suggested metric names/semantics: 
- redwood.export.queued_bytes (gauge)
- redwood.export.backlog_bytes (gauge)
- redwood.export.attempts (counter)
- redwood.export.successes (counter)
- redwood.export.last_handshake_epoch (gauge)

mike: perfect. For quotas we need a per-tenant time-series (daily bytes) + an alert when usage > 90% of committed quota. Can the agents compute daily delta or should backend do it?

tom: backend will compute authoritative quotas but agent-side aggregation reduces noise. Agent emits delta; backend aggregates and enforces. We'll include a reconciliation job to fix drift.

leo: audit log action items: 1) define audit schema, 2) log entry on each successful KMS signing, 3) log on handshake failure, 4) ensure entries are signed and timestamped. I'll draft schema.

anya: I'll start a quick devex draft dashboard (JSON) and link it in #docs once ready. Want columns: tenant, status, last_export, daily_usage, quota_pct, last_kms_sig.

sara: thanks everyone. Action items: dan/leo -> produce proxy + kms design doc; jana/tom -> metric naming + aggregation contract; anya -> dashboard draft; mike -> confirm quota alert thresholds. We'll reconvene Thurs. :thumbsup:
